title: Stored data whose durability does not match its lifetime
rationale: Soroban's three storage durabilities are not interchangeable, and the differences are silent ones. A temporary entry expires and is then reclaimed: there is no archive and no restore, so a balance written there does not become missing, it becomes zero the next time it is read. Persistent entries expire too, but they are archived and can be restored, which is why they are the only place a balance belongs. And instance storage is a single entry loaded with the contract on every invocation, so per-account data written there grows without bound and is paid for by every unrelated call. Both mistakes type-check, both pass a test suite that never advances the ledger past a TTL, and neither is visible to general Rust tooling. The check reads the name of the key being written, using a word list of names that mean durable data (`balance`, `supply`, `admin`) and names that mean per-account data, because without types or a schema there is nothing else to compare against — so it is a heuristic, and a key called `K1` is not analysed at all.
remediation: Put balances, allowances, supply and administrative addresses in `persistent` storage, and extend their TTL on the paths that touch them. Put contract-wide configuration — a fee, a pause flag, a version — in `instance` storage. Put nonces and other data that is worthless once it expires in `temporary` storage, which is what it is for.
